models.name: multi_user_todo_guests
models.description:
Temporary guest accounts for unauthenticated users during registration and login flows.

This table stores guest user identities that are created during the authentication process. Guest accounts serve as temporary placeholders for users who are in the process of registering or logging in. Each guest account has email authentication credentials and can establish sessions for temporary access.

Guest accounts are typically short-lived and may be automatically cleaned up after successful registration or login completion. They provide a way to track unauthenticated user activity while maintaining proper authentication flow separation.

Relationships:
- Has many {@link multi_user_todo_guest_sessions} for temporary access
- References {@link multi_user_todo_audit_logs} for security tracking
- May be converted to {@link multi_user_todo_members} upon successful registration

plainFields.name: email
plainFields.description: Unique email address for guest authentication and identification.

plainFields.name: password_hash
plainFields.description: Hashed password for guest account security.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the guest account was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the guest account was last updated.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the guest account was soft-deleted, null if active.

models.name: multi_user_todo_guest_sessions

foreignFields.name: multi_user_todo_guest_id
foreignFields.description: Guest account associated with this session. {@link multi_user_todo_guests.id}

plainFields.name: ip

plainFields.name: href
plainFields.description: Current page URL where the session was created for context tracking.

plainFields.name: referrer
plainFields.description: Referrer URL indicating where the user came from for analytics.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the session was created for audit purposes.

plainFields.name: expired_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the session expires for security enforcement.

models.name: multi_user_todo_members
models.description:
Registered user accounts with email/password authentication credentials.

This table stores the core identity and authentication information for registered users of the multi-user Todo application. Each member represents a unique user who can create, manage, and organize their private todo lists. The table includes authentication credentials (email and password hash) along with user profile information.

Users can manage their account settings, including password changes and account deletion. All operations performed by members are tracked through session tables and audit logs. Members have complete privacy isolation - they can only access their own todos and cannot view other users' data.

{@link multi_user_todo_member_sessions.id} tracks authentication sessions for this user.
{@link multi_user_todo_member_password_resets.id} handles password recovery workflows.
{@link multi_user_todo_todos.id} contains all todos owned by this user.

plainFields.name: email
plainFields.description: Unique email address used for authentication and account identification.

plainFields.name: password_hash
plainFields.description: Hashed password for secure authentication using industry-standard hashing algorithms.

plainFields.name: display_name
plainFields.description: User's visible name displayed throughout the application interface.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the user account was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the user account was last updated.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the user account was soft-deleted, allowing for account recovery within retention period.

models.name: multi_user_todo_member_sessions
models.description:
JWT session tokens for member authentication with access and refresh support.

This table stores authentication sessions for registered members, tracking their login events and session metadata. Each session contains connection context including IP address, referrer information, and timestamps for session lifecycle management. Sessions are managed through authentication flows and provide the foundation for secure member access to the todo application.

The table maintains an audit trail of member login activity and supports JWT token management with proper expiration handling. Sessions are append-only records that capture authentication events for security monitoring and user activity tracking.

{@link multi_user_todo_members.id}

foreignFields.name: multi_user_todo_member_id
foreignFields.description: Belonged member's {@link multi_user_todo_members.id}.

plainFields.name: access_token
plainFields.description: JWT access token for member authentication.

plainFields.name: refresh_token
plainFields.description: JWT refresh token for session renewal.

plainFields.name: ip
plainFields.description: IP address of the member's connection.

plainFields.name: href
plainFields.description: Current URL where the session was created.

plainFields.name: referrer
plainFields.description: Referrer URL that directed the member to the application.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the session was created.

plainFields.name: expired_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the session expires.

models.name: multi_user_todo_admins
models.description:
Administrator accounts with email/password authentication and elevated privileges.

This table stores administrator identity information including authentication credentials and profile data. Administrators have elevated system access for management functions including user support, system configuration, and audit oversight.

Each administrator account is associated with session records in {@link multi_user_todo_admin_sessions} for authentication management and password reset tokens in {@link multi_user_todo_admin_password_resets} for account recovery.

plainFields.name: email
plainFields.description: Administrator's unique email address used for authentication.

plainFields.name: password_hash
plainFields.description: Hashed password for administrator authentication.

plainFields.name: display_name
plainFields.description: Administrator's display name for system identification.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the administrator account was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the administrator account was last updated.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the administrator account was soft-deleted, or null if active.

models.name: multi_user_todo_admin_sessions
models.description:
JWT session tokens for administrator authentication with access and refresh support.

This table manages administrator login sessions, storing authentication tokens and connection context for secure access control. Each session is tied to a specific administrator account and tracks login metadata including IP address, user agent, and expiration timestamps. Sessions support both access and refresh token functionality with proper expiration handling.

The table follows the standard session pattern with foreign key relationship to {@link multi_user_todo_admins} for administrator identity verification. Sessions are managed through authentication flows and provide audit trail capabilities for security monitoring.

foreignFields.name: multi_user_todo_admin_id
foreignFields.description: Belonged administrator's {@link multi_user_todo_admins.id}.

plainFields.name: access_token
plainFields.description: JWT access token for authentication.

plainFields.name: refresh_token
plainFields.description: JWT refresh token for token renewal.

plainFields.name: ip
plainFields.description: IP address of the session connection.

plainFields.name: href
plainFields.description: URL of the session initiation.

plainFields.name: referrer
plainFields.description: HTTP referrer header value.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Session creation timestamp.

plainFields.name: expired_at
plainFields.description: Session expiration timestamp.

models.name: multi_user_todo_admin_password_resets
models.description:
Password reset tokens with expiration for administrator account recovery.

This table stores temporary password reset tokens that allow administrators to securely reset their account passwords. Each token is valid for a limited time period and can only be used once. The tokens are generated during password reset requests and verified during the reset process.

Tokens are associated with specific administrator accounts and include security features like expiration tracking and usage status to prevent unauthorized access. The table maintains a complete audit trail of password reset attempts for security monitoring.

Related entities: {@link multi_user_todo_admins} for administrator account reference, {@link multi_user_todo_admin_sessions} for authentication context.

foreignFields.name: multi_user_todo_admin_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the administrator account requesting password reset. {@link multi_user_todo_admins.id}

plainFields.name: token
plainFields.description: Secure password reset token used for account recovery verification.

plainFields.name: expires_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the reset token expires and becomes invalid.

plainFields.name: used_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the reset token was successfully used, marking it as consumed.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the reset token was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the reset token record was last updated.

models.name: multi_user_todo_member_password_resets
models.description:
Password reset tokens with expiration for member account recovery.

This table stores temporary password reset tokens that allow members to securely reset their passwords. Each token has a limited validity period and can only be used once. The tokens are generated when members request password resets and are invalidated after successful password changes or expiration.

Tokens reference the member who requested the reset and include security features like expiration timestamps to prevent unauthorized access. This table supports the password recovery workflow described in the authentication requirements.

Related to {@link multi_user_todo_members} for member identity and authentication context.

foreignFields.name: multi_user_todo_member_id
foreignFields.description: Member who requested the password reset. {@link multi_user_todo_members.id}.

plainFields.name: token
plainFields.description: Unique reset token used for password recovery authentication.

plainFields.name: expires_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the reset token expires and becomes invalid.

plainFields.name: used_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the token was successfully used for password reset. Null if unused.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the reset token was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the reset token record was last updated.

models.name: multi_user_todo_audit_logs
models.description:
System-wide audit trail capturing all user operations and system events for security monitoring and compliance.

This table serves as the central repository for audit data across the entire application. It records every significant operation performed by users (members, admins, guests) as well as system-generated events. Each entry captures the actor who performed the action, the type of event, timestamp, IP address, user agent, and detailed payload of the operation.

The audit trail supports security investigations, compliance reporting, and operational monitoring. Records are append-only and should never be modified once created to maintain audit integrity. {@link multi_user_todo_members.id} and {@link multi_user_todo_admins.id} are referenced when actions are performed by authenticated users.

Audit entries are categorized by event type (user_login, todo_created, todo_updated, etc.) and tagged with success/failure status to help identify security incidents and operational issues.

foreignFields.name: multi_user_todo_member_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the member who performed this action, if applicable. {@link multi_user_todo_members.id}.

foreignFields.name: multi_user_todo_admin_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the admin who performed this action, if applicable. {@link multi_user_todo_admins.id}.

plainFields.name: actor_type
plainFields.description: Type of actor who performed the action: 'member', 'admin', 'guest', or 'system'.

plainFields.name: event_type
plainFields.description: Category of the audit event (e.g., 'user_login', 'todo_created', 'todo_updated', 'system_event').

plainFields.name: ip_address
plainFields.description: IP address from which the action was performed for security tracking.

plainFields.name: user_agent
plainFields.description: User agent string of the client that performed the action.

plainFields.name: success_flag
plainFields.description: Whether the operation completed successfully or encountered an error.

plainFields.name: details
plainFields.description: JSON payload containing event-specific details and parameters.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the audit entry was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the audit entry was last updated (typically matches created_at for audit integrity).

models.name: multi_user_todo_system_configurations
models.description:
System-wide configuration settings and parameters that control application behavior.

Stores key-value pairs for system configuration with support for different scopes (global, component-specific, environment-specific). Each configuration entry includes type information for validation and version tracking for audit purposes. System administrators manage these configurations to control application behavior, feature flags, and operational parameters.

Configuration changes are tracked through temporal fields, allowing rollback and audit trail capabilities. The table supports hierarchical configuration with inheritance from global to specific scopes.

plainFields.name: config_key
plainFields.description: Unique identifier for the configuration parameter. Used to reference the setting in code.

plainFields.name: config_value
plainFields.description: String representation of the configuration value. May contain JSON for complex configurations.

plainFields.name: data_type
plainFields.description: Data type of the configuration value for validation purposes. Examples: 'string', 'number', 'boolean', 'json'.

plainFields.name: scope
plainFields.description: Scope of the configuration (global, component, environment). Determines applicability.

plainFields.name: description
plainFields.description: Human-readable description of what this configuration controls.

plainFields.name: is_active
plainFields.description: Whether this configuration is currently active and being used by the system.

plainFields.name: version
plainFields.description: Version number for configuration tracking and rollback capabilities.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this configuration was first created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this configuration was last modified.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this configuration was soft-deleted (if applicable).

models.name: multi_user_todo_performance_metrics
models.description:
System performance monitoring data and metrics collection for the multi-user todo application.

This table captures various performance indicators including response times, throughput metrics, resource utilization, and system health measurements. Each record represents a single performance measurement event collected at a specific timestamp.

Performance metrics are used for system monitoring, capacity planning, and identifying performance bottlenecks. The data supports operational dashboards, alerting systems, and performance trend analysis.

Relationships:
- References system configurations for metric collection settings
- Supports uptime monitoring with performance context
- Provides data for audit trail correlation
- Enables error analysis with performance context

plainFields.name: endpoint_path

plainFields.name: collection_timestamp
plainFields.description: Exact timestamp when this performance metric was collected.

plainFields.name: created_at

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this performance record was last updated.

models.name: multi_user_todo_uptime_monitorings
models.description:
Service availability tracking and uptime statistics for system monitoring.

This table records periodic service health checks and availability metrics for monitoring system reliability. It captures response times, service status, and uptime calculations to provide comprehensive visibility into system performance and availability.

Each record represents a single monitoring check performed at a specific interval, allowing for historical trend analysis and SLA compliance tracking. The data supports alerting systems and performance dashboards.

models.name: multi_user_todo_error_logs
models.description:
System-wide error logging and exception tracking for the multi-user Todo application.

This table captures detailed error information including error type, message, stack trace, severity level, and contextual metadata. It supports error analysis, monitoring, and debugging workflows by providing comprehensive error tracking capabilities.

Each error log entry records the error occurrence timestamp, error details, and optional user/session context for error attribution. The table supports classification by error type and severity for prioritized error handling and analysis.

Key relationships:
- Optional reference to user sessions for error attribution
- Supports error categorization by type and severity
- Enables error trend analysis and monitoring

This infrastructure table is essential for maintaining system reliability and providing diagnostic capabilities for production issues.

models.name: multi_user_todo_system_maintenance_logs
models.description:
System maintenance log tracking all administrative operations and maintenance activities.

This table serves as the central audit trail for system maintenance operations performed by administrators. It captures details about maintenance tasks such as database backups, system updates, configuration changes, and other administrative activities. Each entry includes the operation type, description, status, and timing information for comprehensive system administration tracking.

The logs are used for auditing maintenance activities, troubleshooting system issues, and ensuring compliance with operational procedures. Maintenance operations are typically initiated by administrators through system management interfaces and recorded here for historical reference.

plainFields.name: status

plainFields.name: started_at

plainFields.name: completed_at

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the maintenance log entry was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the maintenance log entry was last updated.

models.name: multi_user_todo_data_retention_policies
models.description:
Data retention rules and archival policies for system entities.

This table defines retention periods, archival strategies, and deletion policies for different types of data within the multi-user todo application. Each policy specifies how long data should be retained before archival or deletion, and under what conditions retention rules apply.

Policies can target specific entity types (todos, edit histories, audit logs, etc.) and define different retention periods based on business requirements and compliance needs. The system uses these policies to automatically manage data lifecycle and ensure proper data governance.

plainFields.name: policy_name

plainFields.name: target_entity_type

plainFields.name: archival_strategy

plainFields.name: description

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the policy was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the policy was last updated.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the policy was soft-deleted.

models.name: multi_user_todo_backup_logs
models.description:
Tracks backup operations and recovery point management for the multi-user todo application.

This table maintains a complete audit trail of all backup operations performed by the system, including scheduled backups, manual backups, and recovery operations. Each entry records the backup type, status, timestamps, file locations, and recovery point information for disaster recovery purposes.

The backup logs are essential for system administrators to monitor backup health, track recovery points, and ensure data protection compliance. They provide visibility into backup success rates, operation durations, and recovery point availability for business continuity planning.

Backup operations reference {@link multi_user_todo_data_retention_policies} for retention rules and {@link multi_user_todo_system_configurations} for backup configuration settings. Recovery operations use these logs to identify available recovery points and their corresponding backup files.

plainFields.name: recovery_point_id

plainFields.name: recovery_point_timestamp

plainFields.name: error_message

plainFields.name: updated_at

models.name: multi_user_todo_todos
models.description:
Main table storing all active todo items with their core properties and ownership information.

This table represents the central business entity of the todo application, containing all active todo items that users create, view, edit, and manage. Each todo belongs to exactly one member user and maintains its current state including title, description, scheduling dates, and completion status.

Todos support soft deletion through the deleted_at field, allowing users to restore items from trash. The table tracks creation and modification timestamps for audit purposes and supports various filtering and sorting operations through appropriate indexing.

Key relationships:
- Each todo belongs to a member user ({@link multi_user_todo_members.id})
- Completion status changes are tracked in a separate table ({@link multi_user_todo_todo_completion_statuses})
- Deleted todos are moved to trash entries ({@link multi_user_todo_todo_trash_entries})
- Edit history is maintained in the EditHistory component
- Snapshots provide point-in-time state capture ({@link multi_user_todo_todo_snapshots})

foreignFields.name: multi_user_todo_member_id
foreignFields.description: Owner member's {@link multi_user_todo_members.id}.

plainFields.name: title
plainFields.description: The main title or name of the todo item. This is the primary identifier that users see in todo lists.

plainFields.name: description
plainFields.description: Optional detailed description providing additional context about the todo item. Can be left empty if not needed.

plainFields.name: start_date
plainFields.description: Optional scheduled start date for when work on the todo should begin. Used for sorting and filtering operations.

plainFields.name: due_date
plainFields.description: Optional deadline date for when the todo should be completed. Used for sorting and filtering operations.

plainFields.name: is_completed
plainFields.description: Indicates whether the todo has been marked as complete. Defaults to false for new todos.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the todo was originally created. Used for sorting and audit purposes.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the todo was last modified. Updated on every edit operation.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the todo was soft-deleted. Null indicates the todo is active.

models.name: multi_user_todo_todo_trash_entries
models.description:
Stores soft-deleted todos that can be restored or permanently deleted. This table serves as the trash management system, allowing users to recover accidentally deleted todos or permanently remove them from the system.

Each entry represents a todo that has been soft-deleted from the active todo list. The original todo data is preserved here until either restored to active status or permanently deleted. This enables the trash functionality where users can view their deleted todos, restore them, or permanently remove them.

Relationships:
- References the original {@link multi_user_todo_todos} through foreign key
- Managed through parent todo operations rather than independent API endpoints

foreignFields.name: multi_user_todo_todo_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the original todo that was soft-deleted. {@link multi_user_todo_todos.id}.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the todo was moved to trash. Used for sorting and filtering trash entries.

plainFields.name: restored_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the todo was restored from trash. Null if still in trash.

plainFields.name: permanently_deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the todo was permanently deleted from trash. Null if still recoverable.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Creation timestamp for audit trail.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Last update timestamp for audit trail.

models.name: multi_user_todo_todo_snapshots
models.description:
Point-in-time snapshots of todos for audit and recovery purposes.

This table captures the complete state of a todo at specific moments in time, 
providing a historical record for audit trails and recovery scenarios. Each 
snapshot represents a frozen state of a todo, including all its properties 
(title, description, start date, due date, completion status) as they existed 
at the time of capture. Snapshots are immutable records that support 
rollback capabilities and change tracking.

Snapshots are typically created during significant todo lifecycle events such 
as edits, completions, or restorations from trash. They enable users to view 
historical states of their todos and support system-level audit requirements.

Relationships:
- Each snapshot belongs to exactly one todo ({@link multi_user_todo_todos.id})
- Todos can have multiple snapshots over their lifecycle
- Snapshots reference the todo they capture at creation time

foreignFields.name: multi_user_todo_todo_id
foreignFields.description: The todo that this snapshot captures. {@link multi_user_todo_todos.id}.

plainFields.name: title
plainFields.description: The title of the todo at the time of snapshot creation.

plainFields.name: description
plainFields.description: The description of the todo at the time of snapshot creation, if present.

plainFields.name: start_date
plainFields.description: The start date of the todo at the time of snapshot creation, if set.

plainFields.name: due_date
plainFields.description: The due date of the todo at the time of snapshot creation, if set.

plainFields.name: is_completed
plainFields.description: The completion status of the todo at the time of snapshot creation.

plainFields.name: is_deleted
plainFields.description: Whether the todo was deleted at the time of snapshot creation.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this snapshot was created.

models.name: multi_user_todo_todo_filter_settings
models.description:
Stores user-defined filter configurations for quick todo list filtering.

Each saved filter configuration allows users to quickly apply their preferred filtering settings without manually selecting options each time. Filters can be configured for completion status (all, complete, incomplete) and other filtering criteria as the application evolves.

Users can create, update, and delete their own filter settings. Each filter setting belongs to exactly one user {@link multi_user_todo_members.id} and is managed through the user's profile settings.

foreignFields.name: multi_user_todo_member_id
foreignFields.description: Owner of this filter configuration. {@link multi_user_todo_members.id}.

plainFields.name: name
plainFields.description: User-friendly name for this saved filter configuration.

plainFields.name: filter_type
plainFields.description: Type of filter being saved (e.g., 'completion_status', 'date_range', 'priority').

plainFields.name: is_default
plainFields.description: Whether this filter should be applied by default when viewing todos.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: When this filter configuration was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: When this filter configuration was last modified.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: When this filter configuration was soft-deleted.

models.name: multi_user_todo_todo_view_stats
models.description:
Tracks usage statistics and view counts for todo management analytics.

This table records each view event when users access their todo lists or individual todo details. Each entry represents a single view operation, capturing the user who performed the view, the todo being viewed (if applicable), and the timestamp of the view. This data supports analytics on user engagement patterns, popular todo management features, and usage trends over time.

The statistics help identify which todo management features are most frequently used and when users are most active with their todo lists. This information can inform UI improvements, feature prioritization, and performance optimization decisions.

Relationships:
- References {@link multi_user_todo_members.id} for user context
- References {@link multi_user_todo_todos.id} for todo context (when viewing individual todos)
- Part of the Todo component analytics subsystem

foreignFields.name: multi_user_todo_member_id
foreignFields.description: User who performed the view operation. {@link multi_user_todo_members.id}.

foreignFields.name: multi_user_todo_todo_id
foreignFields.description: Todo being viewed (null for list views). {@link multi_user_todo_todos.id}.

plainFields.name: view_type
plainFields.description: Type of view operation performed: 'list' for todo list views, 'detail' for individual todo views.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the view operation occurred.

models.name: multi_user_todo_todo_completion_statuses
models.description:
Tracks completion status changes for todos with timestamps for audit purposes.

Each record represents a single status change event when a todo is marked as complete or incomplete. This provides a complete audit trail of completion status transitions over time, allowing users to see when their todos were completed and potentially when they were marked incomplete again.

The table maintains referential integrity with the main {@link multi_user_todo_todos} table and ensures that every status change is recorded with precise timing information for accountability and historical tracking.

foreignFields.name: multi_user_todo_todo_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the todo whose completion status changed. {@link multi_user_todo_todos.id}.

plainFields.name: is_completed
plainFields.description: Whether the todo was marked as completed (true) or incomplete (false) in this status change.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the completion status change occurred.

models.name: multi_user_todo_todo_sorting_preferences
models.description:
Stores user preferences for default todo list sorting methods and directions.

Each user can configure their preferred sorting method (creation date, start date, or due date) and direction (ascending or descending) for their todo list view. These preferences are applied by default when users view their todo lists unless overridden by temporary sorting selections.

This table maintains a 1:1 relationship with {@link multi_user_todo_members} through a unique constraint on the member foreign key, ensuring each user has exactly one sorting preference setting.

foreignFields.name: multi_user_todo_member_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the member who owns these sorting preferences. {@link multi_user_todo_members.id}.

plainFields.name: sorting_method
plainFields.description: Preferred sorting method for todo lists. Valid values: 'creation_date', 'start_date', 'due_date'.

plainFields.name: sorting_direction
plainFields.description: Sorting direction preference. True for ascending, false for descending.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the sorting preference was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the sorting preference was last updated.

models.name: multi_user_todo_todo_filter_setting_values
models.description:
Stores individual filter configuration values as key-value pairs for proper 1NF normalization.

Each record represents a single filter setting value associated with a specific filter configuration. This table ensures atomic values and eliminates repeating groups that would violate First Normal Form if stored directly in the parent filter settings table.

The key-value structure allows flexible filter configuration while maintaining data integrity through proper normalization. Values are stored with appropriate data types based on the filter configuration requirements.

This table supports the filter functionality by providing granular control over individual filter parameters and their values. {@link multi_user_todo_todo_filter_settings.id}

foreignFields.name: multi_user_todo_todo_filter_setting_id
foreignFields.description: Parent filter setting configuration. {@link multi_user_todo_todo_filter_settings.id}

plainFields.name: key
plainFields.description: Filter parameter key identifying the specific filter setting type.

plainFields.name: value
plainFields.description: Filter parameter value stored as string for flexibility across different filter types.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this filter setting value was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this filter setting value was last updated.

models.name: multi_user_todo_edit_histories
models.description:
Main edit history entries recording each todo modification event.

Each entry represents a single edit operation performed on a todo, capturing the timestamp and user who made the change. This table serves as the central audit trail for tracking todo modifications over time.

Edit history entries are created whenever a user modifies a todo's title, description, start date, or due date. The granular field-level changes are tracked in {@link multi_user_todo_edit_history_field_changes} for detailed audit capabilities.

Relationships:
- References the {@link multi_user_todo_todos} table to identify which todo was edited
- References the {@link multi_user_todo_members} table to identify who made the edit
- Has many field change records in {@link multi_user_todo_edit_history_field_changes}
- Has snapshot records in {@link multi_user_todo_edit_history_snapshots} for point-in-time state capture

foreignFields.name: multi_user_todo_todo_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the todo that was edited. {@link multi_user_todo_todos.id}.

foreignFields.name: multi_user_todo_member_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the user who made the edit. {@link multi_user_todo_members.id}.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the edit was performed.

models.name: multi_user_todo_edit_history_field_changes
models.description:
Tracks individual field changes within each edit history entry for granular audit trail.

Each record represents a specific field modification made during a todo edit operation. This table captures the field name, previous value, and new value for each changed field, providing detailed audit information for compliance and debugging purposes.

This table is subsidiary to {@link multi_user_todo_edit_histories} and provides the granular field-level tracking required by the edit history functionality.

foreignFields.name: multi_user_todo_edit_history_id
foreignFields.description: Parent edit history entry that contains this field change. {@link multi_user_todo_edit_histories.id}.

plainFields.name: field_name
plainFields.description: Name of the field that was modified (e.g., 'title', 'description', 'start_date', 'due_date').

plainFields.name: previous_value
plainFields.description: The value of the field before the edit operation. Stored as string for flexibility across different field types.

plainFields.name: new_value
plainFields.description: The value of the field after the edit operation. Stored as string for flexibility across different field types.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this field change was recorded.

models.name: multi_user_todo_edit_history_snapshots
models.description:
Point-in-time snapshots of todo state for audit trail completeness.

This table captures the complete state of a todo at specific moments in time,
providing a historical record for audit purposes. Each snapshot represents
the exact state of a todo when a significant event occurred, such as before
and after major edits or at regular intervals for compliance tracking.

Snapshots are append-only and serve as immutable records of todo evolution
over time. They complement the granular edit history by providing complete
state captures rather than incremental changes.

Related entities: {@link multi_user_todo_todos} for the todo being snapshotted,
{@link multi_user_todo_edit_histories} for detailed change tracking.

foreignFields.name: multi_user_todo_todo_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the todo being snapshotted. {@link multi_user_todo_todos.id}

plainFields.name: title
plainFields.description: The title of the todo at the time of snapshot.

plainFields.name: description
plainFields.description: The description of the todo at the time of snapshot.

plainFields.name: start_date
plainFields.description: The start date of the todo at the time of snapshot.

plainFields.name: due_date
plainFields.description: The due date of the todo at the time of snapshot.

plainFields.name: is_completed
plainFields.description: The completion status of the todo at the time of snapshot.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this snapshot was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this snapshot was last updated. Required for temporal tracking compliance.
